title: Lean verification of the Riemann Hypothesis

quotes.text: We hereby certify that both the statement and the proof of the Riemann Hypothesis are correct.
quotes.for: The communities certify both the theorem statement and its proof.

quotes.text: The checkers con-leche and con-ron come with a formal proof, relative to set theory, that they cannot accept a false proof, thus addressing concerns that Lean's logic itself might have flaws that the proof could exploit.
quotes.for: Soundness guarantees of the con-leche and con-ron independent checkers.
Publication timestamp of the Lean and Mathlib communities' certification statement.

quotes.text: Joint statement by the Lean and Mathlib communities, endorsed by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative.
quotes.for: Endorsement of the joint verification statement by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative.

quotes.text: On November 20, 2026, Levent Alpöge released a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis as a Lean library comprising 17 million lines of code.
quotes.for: November 20, 2026 release date and 17 million lines of Lean code.

quotes.text: The codebase depends directly only on Mathlib. Over the past day, the Lean and Mathlib communities have rallied to verify the proof's correctness.
quotes.for: The library depends directly only on Mathlib.

quotes.text: By now, dozens of people have reported correct compilation of the codebase, reproducing the same raw proof export file.
quotes.for: Independent compilation reproducing the same exported proof.

quotes.text: That statement was compared against the theorem proved by Alpöge using two independent tools (comparator and con-leche --compare), both confirming that the theorem proved in Alpöge's library is exactly Mathlib's statement of the Riemann Hypothesis.
quotes.for: Comparison tools confirming Alpöge's theorem matches Mathlib's Riemann hypothesis definition.

quotes.text: These checks ran on an inert export of the proof, out of reach of hypothetical malicious code in the Lean proof sources.
quotes.for: Verification checks running on an inert proof export insulated from malicious source code.

title: A remark on the Riemann Hypothesis

quotes.text: Claude and I have also formalized the arguments without assumptions.
quotes.for: Alpöge attributes the formalized argument to his collaboration with Claude.

quotes.text: The precise timing is horrible. If I could have, I'd have finished this all much earlier.
quotes.for: Alpöge calls the release timing horrible in his note.

quotes.text: Claude and I have had a great time together with such breadth in recent months, but this time Claude far outpaced me near the finish line.
quotes.for: Alpöge describes Claude outpacing him near the end of the proof.

quotes.text: I of course amused myself, and hit 250,000+ pages.
quotes.for: Length of the informal write-up referenced in Alpöge's footnote.

quotes.text: I guided us to the right situation analogous to that toy setting, and then Claude began to leave me in awe.
quotes.for: Alpöge guiding the approach while Claude supplied mathematical advances.

quotes.text: This puts us in the rather extraordinary situation this age has made possible, in which I am presenting the world with a complete argument before having mastered a massive neighbourhood around its mathematics.
quotes.for: Alpöge presenting the formal argument before mastering the surrounding mathematical neighborhood.

quotes.text: I intend to do my best to understand and impart understanding of this argument and its certain simplifications, to speak about it, to write it properly.
quotes.for: Alpöge's intention to understand, explain, and simplify the proof.

title: Verification files for the Lean proof of the Riemann Hypothesis

quotes.text: The published Lean source compiles without errors, the five headline theorems depend only on the three standard axioms
quotes.for: Sutherland reports successful compilation and itemizes verification results.

quotes.text: every module has been replayed through the Lean kernel, two independently written kernels, nanoda and con-leche, accept the full exported proof, and lean4lean accepts every compiled module.
quotes.for: Completed Lean-kernel replays and independent kernel checks on Sutherland's verification page.

quotes.text: Page last updated 2026-11-22 16:20 UTC. Results below are as of that time and this page will be updated as the remaining checks finish.
quotes.for: November 22, 2026 16:20 UTC update timestamp and ongoing status of remaining checks.

quotes.text: All 175,187 modules compile (Lean v4.33.1, Mathlib v4.33.1)
quotes.for: Successful compilation of all 175,187 modules.

quotes.text: The lake comparator run and the Lean-kernel replay of the export are still in progress.
quotes.for: Distinction between completed checks and ongoing Lean-kernel export replays.

quotes.text: statement comparison and axiom check passed; final kernel replay in progress (single-threaded on a 62 GB export).
quotes.for: Single-threaded lake comparator kernel replay in progress on the 62 GB export.

quotes.text: "GRH" here means Dirichlet L-functions: all moduli and all characters. Dedekind zeta functions, Hecke L-functions and automorphic L-functions in general are not among the statements that were checked.
quotes.for: Scope of verified Generalized Riemann Hypothesis limited to Dirichlet L-functions.

quotes.text: The Riemann hypothesis tells us about the deviation from the average.
quotes.for: The significance of the hypothesis for the distribution of primes.

quotes.text: Formulated in Riemann's 1859 paper, it asserts that all the 'non-obvious' zeros of the zeta function are complex numbers with real part 1/2.
quotes.for: Clay Mathematics Institute's description of the Riemann hypothesis and real part 1/2.

quotes.for: Thomas Bloom cautions against expecting immediate practical applications.

title: Rules for the Millennium Prize Problems

quotes.text: CMI has designated a $7 million prize fund for the solutions to these Problems, with $1 million allocated to each Problem
quotes.for: The $1 million prize allocated to each Millennium Prize Problem.

quotes.text: CMI does not accept direct submission of proposed solutions.
quotes.for: Clay Mathematics Institute does not accept direct submissions.

quotes.text: Before CMI will consider a proposed solution, all three of the following conditions must be satisfied: (i) the proposed solution must be published in a Qualifying Outlet (see §6), and (ii) at least two years must have passed since publication
quotes.for: Publication in a qualifying outlet and two-year waiting period before Clay consideration.

quotes.text: (iii) the proposed solution must have received general acceptance in the global mathematics community.
quotes.for: Requirement of general acceptance in the global mathematics community.
